body: Hikkaduwa Beach is an absolute gem on Sri Lanka's southwestern coast. The golden sand stretches for miles, perfect for long sunrise walks or sunset lounging. The water is incredibly clear, making it ideal for snorkeling and spotting colorful tropical fish and sea turtles right from the shore.The beach has a wonderful laid-back vibe with plenty of beachfront cafes and restaurants serving fresh seafood. Surfers will love the consistent waves, especially during the season from November to April. The coral reef just offshore creates a natural sanctuary teeming with marine life.Whether you're seeking adventure through water sports, relaxation under swaying palms, or vibrant nightlife, Hikkaduwa delivers. The local community is warm and welcoming, adding to the authentic Sri Lankan experience. It's easily accessible from Colombo and makes for a perfect beach getaway. Highly recommended for families, couples, and solo travelers alike.

body: Hikkadua beach boasts over two miles of surfing paradise and stunning sunsets. The peak season starts in December and runs till the end of April. There are dozens of beachside restaurants, cafes, juice bars, chill out bars, surf schools, diving schools and hotels, guesthouses. Whether you’re visiting for 2-3 days or a fortnight, there is plenty to do. Solo travel, couples or small groups, there’s so much on offer. It’s busy peak season but not too overcrowded. There’s nightlife, water activities to suit all budgets. You really are spoilt for choice. Local transportation connections to Colombo, private hire and not far from Galle Fort. The current is strong so be advised there are constantly red flags on display along the beach. Surfers gravitate here from all over the world. There are tournaments also. I went scuba diving with Blue Deep Diving, very good. Most places cater for tourists, so they will have a local and western menu. The top floor of Riff hotel offers a panoramic view of the whole beach. Sunset is usually 18:15/20 each day. You will burn if you don’t use sunscreen wisely. Temperature is between 27-32 degrees.
title: Something For Everyone.

body: We absolutely LOVE Hikkaduwa beach! This is a really long stretch of beach with some of the softest sand we have ever seen. As beaches go, it's absolutely beautiful.Bear in mind that there are different areas. A long quiet stretch with the occasional peaceful cafe, a section with lots of nice bar / restaurants that are good for sun downer cocktails, but also at one end (where the beach gets thinner) we found that it is not so nice. Much more crowded, poorer quality food places and noisy, trashy bars. We just avoided that part and you wouldn't even know it was there if you didn't walk that far. Just opt for the quieter side and you're in for a real treat. You can always walk down that way if you really want to. You can swim here, but be aware of occasional big waves. Ask locals to point out safe areas. Surfing here is very popular. SINGLE GIRLS - Do be aware that we heard of several cases where sleazy surf instructors had groped girls or asked inappropriate things. It's a shame. But the reality is that we would advise going in a group just for safety.The beach was a bit dirty during Christmas / NYE. Lots of fireworks were never cleaned up, lots of bottles etc just left. Sad to see. But in our experiences around Asia we have seen far, far worse....There will always be a few negatives if you look hard enough. But on the whole this was definitely our favourite beach on the South / West of Sri Lanka.
title: The best beach in the South West without any doubt.

body: Our family of five, three adults and two children, spent time on and off at Hikkaduwa Beach while staying at Coral Sands Hotel between 25th to 28th December 2019. We were there in the mornings and evenings, walking along the white sandy beach, swimming in the calm, clear blue waters or simply enjoying - sitting and lazing around.Diving and snorkelling gear are available for hire at many locations along the beach. You can swim to the nearby colourful reef to watch and enjoy aquatic life - the many colourful fishes darting around as well as multi-coloured corals. If you are lucky you might come across a turtle too swimming in the waters. Diving and snorkelling were a fabulous pastime for the many visitors frequenting the beach. The calm shallow waters between the reef and the beach was ideal for a leisurely swim. You can quench your thirst at the many juice bars along the beach.We enjoyed the walks along the lovely wide beach with its white sands and getting into the calm waters.The best time to enjoy Hikkaduwa beach is during the non-monsoonal period between November to March.

body: We first stopped for a short time on a tour, but saw that it had a lot to offer so when we had a free day in Columbo we took the two hour train ride to Hikaduwa. (Don't get suckered in to first class like we did, go second. See my other review) the streets are full of shops, bars, restaurants and some street food. We felt adventurous, so got some bbq fish and chicken from a stall at the beach car park. Wow! It's local, authentic, which means the fish is roughly chopped bbq'd sauced and spiced, as is the chicken and served in a cardboard dish. Lots of meat on the fish. Beautiful. Ask for spicy otherwise it will be mild. On to the beach. All manner of water sports on offer; scuba, snorkelling, glass bottom boat, surfing hire, lessons. We just swam and snorkelled in the warm water. At the southern end of the beach large sea turtles are found while wading in the shallow reef. Not sure why they stay there, they don't seem distressed at all the people's attention. Beautiful to watch up close. Lots of coconut vendors and beachfront restaurants. We had lunch at "Parrots paradise" (see other review). Don't forget to have them open the nut after drinking to scrape the flesh.. yum. We also bought a small bottle of calypso white rum from a bottle shop, well worth it to top up the coconut. Beach gets really hot in the middle of the day with not much shade around, so maybe a cafe, restaurant or bar. Morning, terrific. Great day was had. 😃
title: Loved it so much we went back.

body: What I really like about Hikkaduwaa beach is that the beach itself has fabulous, beautiful, clear warm water, and lots of interesting things to see along the shoreline. But along with that is that it’s a town big enough to feel like you are really living among the people and can break out of the tourist scene.Not so much a place to come for nightlife, or at least not that we’ve yet found now on day five, not really looking that hard, but definitely a very nice place to chill lax and observe some Sri Lankan culture.The train ride to get here from Colombo is exceedingly affordable and breathtaking as it runs right along the coast almost the entire way.Once here, it’s very easy to just jump on a passing bus to explore further down the coast line to places like Galle which offers more high-end shopping gorgeous views and lots of interesting history. In addition to tourism, fishing is a primary industry here and another fun thing to do is to go check out where the fishing boats bring their early morning catch and watch all of the locals making their choices.Don’t miss the surrounding neighborhoods and some of the treasures that they hold, small mom-and-pop businesses that offer great value and wonderful experiences. Also don’t miss a place sectioned off on the beach where baby turtles are kept safe beneath the sand until the eggs hatch and they are kept safe from predators until they are able to make their way down to the water.You can swim right up to the sea turtles but please please don’t touch. Touching may seem harmless but chemicals that we carry on our hands, like sunscreen, is very damaging to them. Locals are OK though with you feeding the turtles bits of seaweed which is a thrill to experience even vicariously.I have yet to do it but there is a living coral reef right up near the shore where you can snorkel.
title: Just Right

body: I’m not typically a beach person, I find the more popular beaches to be much the same around the world (packed full of overpriced bars/restaurants etc) but there are some amazing things that set this beach apart from the rest. We headed down to the beach around 8am with the hope of seeing a wild giant sea turtle feeding and we were lucky enough to find one! This was one of our main hopes for this trip as we love animals. There were a couple of people there already and shortly after there were more and more people but they all seemed to be respectful and gave the turtle space to do as it pleased. There are some officials who “police” the area so they would stop anyone from touching the turtle etc. Having been amazed by the turtle we then used our own snorkel in the shallows and it was full of various fish and other marine life , there were plenty of people offering snorkel tours to a close by rock (by boat) which we may do tomorrow. We walked up the beach and stopped at a place for some breakfast, it was average but we just needed to eat something. There’s plenty of choice for food but I’ve found that the better places are a short walk inland from the seafront. We went back to our room to top up our sun cream and headed back to the beach where we had a drink in the shade before renting some body boards and having some fun in the waves! The waves are very strong so I would not let children play in the sea without an accompanying adult!Although I’m not a fan of beaches in general I found it was rich in marine life which was incredible to see and the body boards were 300 rupees each for an hour which seemed like good value.
title: Busy, commercial but a lot to do

body: Hikkaduwa are most nice one of beach in sri lanka... you can visit to see there turtle on the ocean..

body: Came here on the train from Mirissa having heard good things. Instantly disappointed. Outside our hotel, that’s another review in itself, Coral Sands hotel (a relic of a bygone era with some relics still coming to holiday each year).Hikkaduwa beach is littered with rubbish and the water in some parts is full of boats so it makes it very difficult to swim. The beach front itself is littered with beach bars most of which are terribly overpriced and people constantly try to sell you either clothes or other trinkets when you are trying to relax. The atmosphere on the beach is nowhere near as chilled as Mirissa. Another horrific experience was watching people poking and prodding the sea turtles. Leave the bloody things alone!!!There are plenty of dive resorts and surf schools too but be cautious. I scuba dive in Ireland and looked at two schools, would not go near them. Old tatty BCDs, dirty regulators and old boats. Nah cheers mate!The surf schools will rent you a board no problem but don’t expect much from them in terms of a surf report, we just got told “um yes loads of waves”. Nothing about reefs, rips of good spots. Also be cautious of local surfers, they have a tendency to drop in on you even if you have caught the wave.We were told by a surf school “no rocks all sand” but my girlfriend was wiped out and hit her foot on a shallow reef. Now I knew about the reef but the guy in the school assured me, “not to worry, very deep”. Not knowing the topography of the sea I expected the school to inform me having never surfed the area before. In short if you have been to Mirissa before here or are planning to go to Mirissa before Hikkaduwa then stay away. In classic Irish terms “this place is a bleedin’ Kip!!!”
title: Stay in Mirissa...awful beach...

body: Great beach, particularly for surfers although main break attracts beginners who tend to spoil surfing for those who can already surf. body: We stayed at the Hikka Tranz by Cinnamon .The hotel was a bit tired it really needs an up grade. It caters for a large group of tourists and I felt a bit overwhelmed with how many people stay at this hotel. No individual treatment .The beach was quite good with the locals cashing in on taking you out to the rocks for snorkelling. Not much coral but some fish life.

body: Great beaches, plenty of good bars and restaurants. The curry bowl guest house is cheap and clean, worth considering as a base.

body: Quite, clean and easy access to see colourful fishes; Snorkeling or Glass boat. Numerous restaurants and bars are located along the entire stretch of the beach.
title: Quite, clean and easy access to see colourful fishes; Snorkeling or Glass boat

body: It's not the prettiest beach. There's some pretty good snorkelling at the northern end - we just wish we had taken flippers because the current was pushing us around. Lion fish, cuttlefish, reef sharks and turtles were the highlights. On the southern end there's a spot where all the tourists gather to feed one or two local turtles. It's a bit pushy shovy as people clamour for the best instagram shots. Would be a bit nicer if people wouldn't grab the turtles either. Other than that, usual beach things to do - bars, restaurants, surf, jetski, boat tours etc. Nice sunset too though.
title: Good snorkelling, average beach.

body: This is a lovely beach that is totally spoilt by the awful way people treat the turtles. They are wild animals not there to be mounted and ridden, coerced onto the beach, or stalked through the water for hours (yes some individuals wouldn’t leave them alone for hours). It would be great if the initiative could be taken in the spots where they do appear frequently for signs to remind people of this. And for beach goers to educate themselves on how to treat wildlife appropriately. Enjoy the turtles from a respectful distance whether snorkelling or paddling.. More about the beach:As is often in Sri Lanka the waves are rough, something to bear in mind if you have little ones. But they are fine if you’re a fairly good swimmer. You can find some good spots for sunbathing at points along the beach. There are the occasional littered areas in between. We walked home as the sun was going down to a nice sunset and impressive lightning on the horizon. As the beach isn’t one long strip it makes an interesting walk round all the bends. We enjoyed ourselves.
title: Turtles deserve better than to be pressed against your speedo, sir.

body: Great beach, just over two hours from Colombo airport. Great place for diving, snorkelling, surfing and generally chilling out. Stays are comfortable, people are warm and friendly and the seafood is exceptional.
title: Peaceful, quaint beach

body: I spent eight Wonderful days Walking, Sunbathing, Boggie Boarding and Swimming at Hikkaduwa Beach!! The endless miles of mostly very clean Golden sand beaches and a very Powerful Crashing Ocean surf!! Great beach bars for miles, so many choices!! The Main Reef Guesthouse and restaurant is a wonderful establishment which is where I stayed while in Hikkaduwa. The Chill Space Beach Bar just a few hundred feet away from the Main Reef has an Exciting Saturday night Beach Party with Dancing and disco!! Cheers!! James B. Oregon USA

body: We stayed near Hikkaduwa beach for a month and this was our sunset point almost everyday and each day it would be better than before!Beach right behind Hikkaduwa trans hotel has few huge turtles visiting every day and one of them is named Rosy by the local guides.If you walk on the beach from here towards north, you can find a reef on the beach at low tide. It’s safe and easy to swim even for beginners!

The beach is also full of rubbish and derbis which no one seems to take responsibility for. Also, touts try selling you everything from massages, coconuts, boat trips, blankets, sight seeing tours, wooden figurines, swimming with turtles....you name it! Not relaxing at all.

body: Having walked down beautiful Adam’s Peak, been mesmerized by the scenery in Ella, soaked in the ambience of Tangalle and Mirissa, Hikkaduwa was not only a huge disappointment, but also felt dreadfully unsafe.Whilst Tangalle and Mirissa were lined with the flora and fauna of Sri Lanka, there were a few coconut trees in Hikkaduwa, but mostly the view is of delapidated, eery, empty hotels. Unlike elsewhere where you could easily get delicious Sri Lankan food for a good price, this place was full of naff restaurants serving expensive Western food, and poor quality at that. Perhaps the most difficult thing is the large groups of local men just wandering around gawking at tourists and in particular hassling women. Having travelled lots of the South for two weeks we expected some people to peddle their wares, but this was constant and at times quite aggressive. At one point whilst I was trying to read my book I had to tell somebody to back away because he was pestering so much. Hardly relaxing.In terms of the tourist population, whilst in other places it was full of backpackers travelling around, here it was mostly what seemed to be people on package deals just here for the beach. Unfortunately, it did give it quite a chavvy vibe and felt somewhat cheap but not cheerful, and not actually even cheap!*Perhaps most distressing was the ‘turtle watching’* Basically, a group of Sri Lankan guys encourage large sea turtles onto the shore (possibly captured and brought in) and feed them seaweed to keep them close. If tourists were to feed them seaweed they have to pay a fee. I gather if they dont pay they get quite intimidating. These tourists then go up to these beautiful creatures and distress them by petting them and taking pictures with them. It really is heartwrenching to see, and astounding how oblivious so many tourists are to how awful this practice is.Sri Lanka has so much beauty and excitement to offer - thank goodness I only spent one day here as it doesn’t show you how great Sri Lanka is. I would discourage anyone from visiting this place.
title: Seedy beach town, horrified by turtle welfare

body: We went to the beach to watch sea turtles and were disgusted by the experience. We went there early morning, to find a group of 4 Sri Lankan men very aggressively asking for money for them to go and get the turtles out of the sea. We stayed there about an hour and this is how it works: those men stay on the beach and ask for money, they make sure you can’t go too close to the water and if a sea turtle tries to come on the beach, they scare it away back to the water to make sure you don’t see it until you pay. One of them had a knuckle duster and showed it to a tourist that was trying to find turtles with some seaweeds. A couple of tourists paid to see one, they took them in the water to make sure the rest of us would not see anything from the beach. The sea was rough and it looked like the couple did not know how to swim and was very uncomfortable, they apparently managed to get a turtle come and say hi to them for 10 sec and that was it. They also tricked some other tourists for paying 200 roupies, and once the turtle was approaching, they asked 2000 roupies. When the tourists said no, that was not the price, then they scared the turtle back to the water. Please do not go and do not pay as it entertains their business!!!
title: Do not go for the turtles

body: Hikkaduwa was a huge disappointment. The ocean was very, very rough and we could not even enter the water in some areas. We visited at the end of July - it is apparently much calmer after December. The sand is not fine and powdery and there was garbage strewn about. Peddlers were plentiful but mainly tolerable; it was the random men who hang around the beach who were very annoying. Hikkaduwa town is dirty, noisy, and chaotic. Walking down the 'sidewalk' or crossing the road is downright dangerous - the buses and other vehicles fly by pedestrians and each other at fairly high speeds in tight quarters. I am surprised there aren't more accidents. The fumes and pollution from vehicles is overwhelming. Proprietors are aggressive. It seems like everyone is trying to get something from you or sell something to you. It's exhausting.I am not sure what tourists see in this place - beauty must really be in the eye of the beholder.
title: Huge disappointment

body: This is a lovely beach to stroll, swim or snorkel. Plenty of outfitters are waiting to guide you, either by paddling out to the reef or swimming with you near the shore. The reef was okay, and getting paddled out there in the long canoe was cool, but really, the fish were better near shore. unfortunately, the coral was destroyed in the tsunami, but there are still fish. We got up-close and personal with two large turtles near shore. It you have even a bit of snorkelling experience, just rent the fins and mask and enjoy the shoreline. People keep dumping bread in the ocean to attract them and they are plentiful, if not too varied.
title: Great beach to walk or snorkel

body: The beach is pretty nice, but there’s not a lot of space to lay down and enjoy the weather. The sea is very rough in August and it’s not very safe to swim. There are also a lot of locals who try to get you on one of those boats with a glass bottom and they won’t stop pushing you until you walk away. Very annoying and not relaxing at all. There are a few reasonably priced restaurants near the coast that are nice.

body: This beach is beautiful, quite a big one and gives amazing views with clear clean water and also lots of water animals towards the other end of the beach. body: The beach is really clean with soft sand. title: Beautiful and diverse

body: We went in the month of June so the place was quiet empty but it was beautiful. Lot of shacks were around
title: Blue water and white sand

body: We fell in love with Sri lanka 2 years ago, and since its only a 4hr flight from Dubai, we go as often as we can. Trying a new beach everytime. Hikkaduwa is bwautifull (not as lovely as Bentota).During our last trip in Hikkaduwa we were walking along the beach at aroumd 8pm in search of a seafood restaurant. As we walked pass the Hikka Tranz hotel, there was a young lady sitting on the beach. A few metres away from her there was a low hanging tree and I saw this Sri Lankan sitting there, watching her, thinking since it was dark he cant be seen. It was eerie. I walked up to the hotel security that was near thr pools,and informed them.We found a restaurant on the beach not far from where we saw this guy hide.Waiting for our food I saw my husband being distracted. A young woman came up from thr beach, looked at the menu and turned back towards the beach to walk back the way she came. My husband jumped up and went to her, spoke to her briefly and she turned back towards the restaurant walking through towards the main rd. Its then that my husbanded pointed out to me a man who was following the girl. When se stopped at the restaurant to view the menu, he walked past just a few steps and stood in the shadows watching her. Luckily my husband was observant and said that he saw them drom a diatance already. While he spoke to the lady, he pointed out the man, who was startled and turned his back.When she walked through the restaurant, he made a dash through the alley way next door to the main road as well. Luckily she got a tuk tuk. I could swear it was the same guy sitting under the bushes at the tree.I was so shaken by it all.So ladies, PLEASE be careful. Dont walk alone on the deserted beaches at night. Please.
title: Ladies be aware

body: I definitely loved Hikkaduwa beach, I don't know how it is during peak season but I was here in July. There wasn't a lot of people and I loved it. It felt like a clean beach to just stroll in and relax in. It was also a good beach to swim in. One side has bigger waves and rocky while the other is sandy. They also have wild turtles swimming here where the locals help you get seaweed to feed the turtles so it will come to shore. I initially saw a crowd of people and asked what was happening. I was curious. I was saddened though that a local approached me and asked for money for me to see the turtle--- they said if i didn't give them money then it wouldn't come to shore. I dive anyway, so I just walked away and let it be. However, they do exist in the area. You can see them naturally in knee length deep, of course, the locals are just trying to get money out of you. I generally loved my whole trip in Sri Lanka --- it felt safe even when I was alone. What I got really tired of though is tuktuk drivers over charging tourists. In Hikkaduwa, the locals would approach me every so often because most were in groups and I was alone. Don't get me wrong, I love mingling---I am a people person. I love meeting new people and I like interacting wiht locals but in Hikkaduwa it was a bit much! I would laze in the beach andthey would sort of wake me to just strike a lot of conversations, usually sales related. Often, a group of french people rescued me because they kept asking about my hotel and if I wanted to come over which of course I didn't. I do love mingling with locals but it just gets a tadbit too muich if they constantly come when you are lazing and resting. I guess, I was a target since most were in groups or couples and I was alone. All else, I still did enjoy Hikkaduwa.
title: Clean Beach During Off Season

body: Hikkaduwa beach is very clean and famous for Coral garden. You can take a glass boat ride to see beautiful corals in the sea. Hikkaduwa beach is situated in Southern province of Sri Lanka near the historical city of Galle.
title: One of the best beach in Sri Lanka

body: Beautiful beach but out of season [July] the sea was very rough and so there were few chances to swim or snorkel.
title: Avoid out of season

body: A beautiful,clean beach and not very crowded unlike other beaches.I went there in the off season so there wasn't much to do.There were a few Locals out there who were getting sea turtles to the shore and we could feed them. You can hire snorkeling gear from the locals and they take you in a boat where you can snorkel. Nice and clean beach and I hope it is always maintained that way.
title: A Very clean beach

body: This is the best beach in the western part of Sri Lanka. You will find less of local crowd and more of foreigners and the beach is much used for snorkeling and scuba dive. There are lot of restaurants by the beach so buy the drink outside and you can enjoy the food having a drink at the beach side restaurants. Hikkaduwa beach has 2 bays- Hikkaduwa bay is small and less waves making it perfect for swimming and Narigama bay which is right next to it more towards the south. This is a spectacular surf beach. You get an amazing sunset viewing opportunity. The Hikkaduwa beach is a very scenic place and a gorgeous tropical beach. The color of the sky and the waves looks amazing and it is a pleasure to the eyes. It is not too crowded. Sea is like a warm bath. It is also clean and active beach and perfect for surfers because of its high waves. You get amazing beach parties at night, just ask around where the party is on a certain day since every day the party is at specific place.There are lots of restaurants and bar options, the sand was soft in most places (few spots of rock found in the water). However watch out for jelly fish, we had a couple of stings. Lots of tourists are found so you don't really need to cover up like in other town. You will find lot of people sun bathing on the clear white sand and almost clear blue waters. It is well worth a trip and the beach is just like a normal holiday beach, water sports, and restaurants etc. When you get off the beach and into town there are many souvenir shops which are fun to browse, and tea stores as well. Best time to visit would be Jan and Feb and from here you can plan for Whale watching. Narigama is a much bigger/longer bay with more restaurants/hotels/activities and bigger waves making it better for surfing. Why don’t you visit Hikkaduwa beach?
title: Hikkaduwa Beach is the Best Beach in the Western part of Sri Lanka Less Waves & Perfect for a Warm Swimming.

body: This is truly a gem of southern Lanka. It has everything for a great vacation. Cozy and comfortable hotels, variety of restaurants and spas. Beautiful beach. Part of the beach, called Narigama, is long and wide, great for swimming, the other part, Hikkaduwa beach, has a coral reef with great snorkeling and scuba diving opportunities. Also, because of coral reef shelter, this beach is suitable for swimming even during summer season when the sea gets really rough. My favorite part of Hikkaduwa, is that its not too commercialized but a cool place with parties and beautiful people from all over the world. Not the resort goers looking to fill their bellies on all inclusive buffets.
title: Perfect beachome for relaxation and recreation

body: I loved this beach for July as we stayed at coral seas... If you go left towards the point you can feed turtles in the mornings. One local guy takes care of them and protects them from tourist that don't treat them with respect... Please give him a tip, he didn't ask for one but after what I saw and how much he loves them he deserves a hefty tip.This beach between coral seas hotel and the point has the best sand beach with gentle waves in July at least. Also a lifeguard on duty and shade trees to sit under.This was our 3rd beach as we started in mirissa, I loved each city for a different reason, this one was my favorite beach for swimming. Mirissa for food, weligama for surfing.
title: My favorite beach on West coast🐢🎴

body: The beach is broad which make it possible to relax for several hours at the beach enjoying the ocean. The beach is not suitable for surfing since the waves breaks very close to shore

body: Beach seemed relatively clean and although it was pretty rough, was in good condition.There seemed to be some more secluded beaches further north, but the tide seemed to come in pretty high.

body: We were out o season so it was quiet. From the various signs, the Russians have found here. The beach is scenic but plastic debris everywhere. The beach is famous for its turtles. A local man sidled up to us keen to show us the turtles. He had a younger companion who entered the sea to entice a turtle to me using seaweed - and it worked - to some extent and I did catch a glimpse of a large turtle close by. Of course these gentlemen wanted to be paid for their time and effort and help the local community. A further (persistent) offer to sample the local Aloe Vera was declined. The beach has many watering holes and we enjoyed some calamari and beer at the end of the morning.
title: Nice beach with turtles

body: The coral reef glass boat ride was an ad-hoc proposal by our local guide as a short activity during our Galle-to-Bentota ride. June is not the best season for sailing far out to areas of better diversity because of the current but we were able to see quite a good variety of marine life including sea turtle on the shallower reef side. There are a few people snorkelling so you can probably see the same things without paying for the ride. However note the sea can get quite choppy, combine that with shallow waters and rocky bottoms, a boat ride is not a bad option if you are interested to see the reef.
title: Coral reef boat rode

body: This was a real eye opener with signs in Russian and Russian menu's but no hassle and clean beach (surprised local Tourist Board/Council still do not pick up the plastic which is surprising as many other beaches have tractor and litter plastic pickers to preserve the major tourist attraction. Great sunsets and good for jogging along the beach when tide is out.
title: Little Russia of Sri Lanka - many tour groups, but clean beach and good food

Mind blowing.

body: On the south of the island, in places like Unawatuna and Hikkaduwa, lie the white sands of the Indian Ocean beaches. A far cry from the green jungles and tea plantations on the mountains. However, all you have to do is take a look around, and if the beach is quiet, it’s easy to imagine yourself as a deserted sailor from centuries ago washing onto an uninhabited island.Sitting on the shoreline, listening to the waves lap up the beach, watching the sky go from yellow, to red, to black, is an extremely relaxing way to end the day.
title: Relaxing way to spend a day in the peace of the ocean

body: This is a must on your travels in sri lanka. The beaches around area are beautiful with lots of swimming snorkelling and surfing to be done. Plus swimming with giant turtles.

body: Our Hotel had entrances directly onto the beach so we took regular strolls along it as well as swam / snorkelled from it.It is a public beach (why not), and there are plenty of people around but it is not unpleasantly crowded.and the food / beverage shacks etc add to the ambience.Yes there are boat vendors etc along the shore, but they generally accept a polite no, and don't hassle you further.We especially liked the area to the North, where most of the locals went (en masse), to enjoy themselves, and seeing them happy, made us happy too.Going into the sea from this beach is very easy and no rubber footwear required,Warning, be vigilant of the many small tourist boats that operate in a most cavalier way in the same area.I snorkelled out lots of times, wearing bright flourescent gear.However, I had to stop many times, and shout loudly at the boat crew, to make them aware of my presence.( they were too busy amusing their customers by doing fast 'doughnuts' in the water and throwing bread over for the fish)This was very unsafe practice and dangerous to swimmers..The authorities, should segregate the boats from swimmers by roped off areas with marker buoys, as they are in many other parts of the world.It is also a great shame to see ignorant people feeding the fish bread etc and feeding / stroking the turtles.too.Titillating as it may be for you, please stop and think, as you are changing the diet and behaviour of the marine life. Thereby, you are quite literally killing them.Maybe some informative notices need to go up along the beach ( and make sure they are in written in the Russian language too ).We still love the place, and would not hesitate to return here at any time.
title: A Lovely Beach ( a bit marred by humans)

body: The beach is nice, and within yards you can see lots of tropical fish if you can snorkel. You don't need anyone's help to see the fish, or for them to be fed. So beware of touts offering trips in glass bottom boats and snorkelling assistance. We got conned because it was our first day in SL. The glass boat was rubbish, you cannot see much through the old glass and there are very few fish in the marine sanctuary part anyway. Then we were kitted out with life jackets and snorkelling gear and lead to the shallow part where locals were playing in the water. There were lots of fish here, but there was no reason to pay someone to see this. Better to bring your own snorkel and enjoy.The rains came and the water became unclear so we did not see the turtles even though we went to the other side of the beach.The guy who was supposed to act as our paid life guard was sitting bored while my kids were in the water - they were not in any danger but I realised he had oversold his credentials. As others have said, the fish and turtles do not belong to locals, so take your own bread to feed them and avoid the useless operators who are trying to hassle and exploit visitors.
title: Nice beach but BEWARE of operators

body: We were told the name is "turtle beach" by our Air BNB owner. We took a tuk tuk in and went to the first part of the beach which had large waves in the afternoon, perfect to jump over, boogie board, and body surf. If you walk down the beach toward the hotel there is a small stone stairway that leads you to another area of the beach. It is more coral and is a little rockier, but it also has sea turtles who will swim in throughout the day. My kids each had a chance to put on a mask and swim along side the gentle creatures. It was an amazing experience. One thing, PLEASE DO NOT TOUCH THE TURTLES. They are wild animals and this can harm them. There was a wonderful local man who spent his day reminding tourist it is not okay to touch the turtles. There were lots of opportunities for snorkeling and diving with a shop on site to rent equipment. The beach was also clean and quiet - great for reading watching the waves, or taking a nap. There are also fruit salesman on the beach. It sounds silly, but it was fun to drink from a coconut and eat fresh pineapple on the beach. We bartered the price down to about 800 rupies - be ready to do that :)

body: This was really a bit of a rip off. With most of the hotels and restaurants jealously commanding their own strip of beach in Hikkaduwa, there are only few places where you can gain free access to the beach. When you do find an access you usually find a fleet of little glass bottomed motor boats waiting to take you for a spin over what remains of the Hikkaduwa coral reef. We took a short 15 minute trip to the edge of the shallow coral reef and although the boat trip was regulated and tickets issued, you may consider it overpriced. The coral reef is very close to the shore and on our trip we were fortunate to see a large turtle as well as some large fish. The coral reef however, is a natural disaster, because much of the coral is dead, due to bleaching in 1998. Damage to the reef is also due to fishing and by boats There are a few signs of it regenerating but it will be many, many years before, if ever, it will return to its former glory. We realized afterwards that the little glass bottomed boat that we used was a contributor to the damage on the reef. The best way of seeing the reef is by snorkeling and you can be guided to the best spots. But be careful of the little glass bottomed boats.
title: Hikkaduwa Reef - A Sad Sight

body: After spending a few days in Negombo our overall impression of Sri Lanka was not great and we were getting a bit frustrated and bored. We decided to take a 2.5 hour cab ride down to Hikkaduwa beach after getting recommendations from locals and other travellers. We stopped by the Turtle Sanctuary which was very cool. We had been told that it was possible to spot turtles in the sea further down Hikkaduwa beach, but that we had to be very lucky to do so - especially if we arrived later in the day.We arrive to Hikkaduwa beach around 10-11am. It was raining as we made our way down to the shore but as soon as we got there we already saw a handful of people in the water, looking at a massive turtle.After having a look from the beach we rented a mask and snorkel for 500LKR each and got in the water. We were amazed! 4-5 massive turtles were calmly swimming around us - the biggest one probably around 1.5m long! Definitely one of the most amazing experiences I’ve ever had. I think the fact that it was raining made a big difference. We were told that the turtles don’t like sunlight and there was also less people swimming.

body: Once you get into Hikkaduwa beach you will find fine golden sand, clear water, good wave action, snorkeling and diving opportunities and beautiful views. There is a little bit of a litter problem but it could easily be rectified if someone took responsibility for clearing it regularly. It’s not at an offensive level at present but is noticeable. The biggest problem I found with this beach is it is so difficult to access. We dropped in to visit on our train trip to Galle. After leaving Hikkaduwa train station we headed to the Galle - Colombo main road along the beach. There we encountered the fishing harbour ( no access to beach) abutting strip shops and continuous cement block walls that meant we had to walk at least 800 m before we could find a lane thru to the beach. Although it’s a tourist town Hikkaduwa is not pedestrian friendly - tuktuks, vans and trucks park over narrow footpaths and make angry gestures or toot horns at pedestrians trying to walk along the shopping strip to shop or get to the beach. Pedestrians are made to feel that they are the lowest priority which is the opposite to most western countries, so it takes some getting used to. Some of the properties along the beach encroach too far onto the beach, leaving less beach for swimmers to set up camp for the day. A lot of businesses that back onto the beach at the port / city end do not open onto the beach and are aesthetically ugly. If the local traders wish to appeal more to tourists then they may need to rethink zoning for businesses along the beach and improve access to the beach. I guess the concrete block wall may be intended as a barrier to flooding but perhaps a stairway or pedestrian bridges could improve beach access. Until access improves I would rate Unawatuna as the best close proximity beach for tourists who are staying in GalleI think Hikkaduwa could be a highly rated beach for tourists, with a few improvements to better accomodate them. I’m saying this from the perspective that I think tourism is an important economic driver and employment focus for this town.

body: We stayed in Hikkaduwa for 3 nights, it was amazing. The beach is calm, water is warm, and you can enjoy a swim. The locals are friendly, sellers wandering the beach do not harass you. A simple ‘no thank you’ will suffice.Towards the Hikka Tranz hotel end of the beach, you get to swim with the turtles. The turtles do not mind the people but tends to get over crowded. For quieter time with the turtles, go visit them in the morning, take few sea plants with you to feed them. You will get great pictures. You can snorkel or swim with them too.To view the corals, you will need to take the boat out into the sea, it is about 10-15 minutes boat ride. Fish comes up right on the beaches. A great place for who are not yet able to snorkel and dive. It is wonderful to see various type of fishes swimming along with you.Along the beach, there are lot of restaurants with various price ranges. All of them seems to be on higher end. Do not forget to put on sun screen, you will get sun burnt very easily. The beach area does not have public shower or restroom. You will need to use your hotel facilities.
title: You will be swimming with the turtles!

body: Hikkaduwa beach with its coral reef is great for beginner snorkellers as its really shallow and the waves are not that bad here. You can see a lot of fish and some corals although the coral reef is still a bit beaten up and the corals are mostly white. Just be careful when the waves are stronger - they may swipe you and toss you on the reef and the scratches and bruises are unpleasant. There are some sellers wandering the beach but they don't usually harass you into buying stuff. Just make sure you have the change when you decide on buying something from them. There are stray dogs running around which may be annoying. You won't enjoy solitude on this beach but it also means that there are services that are not found on more private beaches. body: Just go there and you will see. Reef and sand, and lots of places to relax. Sea life is impressive, so go snorkeling and meet turtles

body: I went over new years with a girlfriend and we had a blast!! Here are some points and tips that might help you:- if you need flip flops or sandals or a towel buy them from an area near the train station. There is a huge market there and you have many options at cheaper rates. I paid 1500slr for a towel and 1600slr for knock off Havanas on the main road just near the beach.- we took the train in from Colombo and it was a great experience...the train is the way to go if you can keep calm and just understand the culture is very different there and there is no sense of personal space. Try to push through to the front of the line for a window seat otherwise youre stuck standing awkwardly. Also there is not much difference between first and second class so go for second class its cheaper! From the train station its a 10 or 15 minute walk to the main strip along the beach...walking was nice because we popped into a few shops on our way to our homestay.- facing the sea the far right towards vibration club was quite dirty the right side was much cleaner. Both the water and the beach area. It was also less busy. There is many places that have wooden sun beds and they say you need to pay but we just sat on them at the sun set coffee bar and no one said anything. - have enough cash i suggest 9000slr a day will be enough. Some days you spend less or more so it balances out. This amount excludes the cost of your accommodation though. But accommodation is cheap and not more than 8000slr a night for a top notch homestay you can find decent places for 3000 to 4500 slr a night.- tuk tuks are everywhere and constantly asking if you want a lift. Be sure to bargain you shouldn't be paying more than 200slr for a ride from one end to the other and most things are in walking distance so no need really. These tuk tuks offer daily rates where you can rent the driver to take you around be sure to haggle and get a deal within your budget. Just finish by saying you don't have enough and walk away most times they just come back to you if not then try with the next guy and increase your budget by a little. - breakfast options are quite limited. Chamis place does a very nice pancake. I highly suggest going there. Good coffee is hard to come across even if you see a lavazza sign it doesn't mean the coffee will be as good as you imagine. - loads of beach restaurants that serve alcohol. I highly suggest sticking to beer or buying your own alcohol from a shop on the main road to take to the restaurant. The cocktails and wines are not the best and can taste quite horrible.- safety was never an issue. We didn't feel threatened or fearful of being robbed but be sure to have your purse on you at all times I suggest a fanny pack kept across your body/shoulder rather than a backpack or daily purse. New Year's eve we had some guys try to drug my drink but luckily I noticed. Be sure to keep an eye on your drink at all times if out of sight just order another. It's typical that when you order a beer order bottle...they bring it unopened and open it at your table.- saw many sunsets but sunrises apparently werent that special so we decided it wasn't worth waking up for- mosquitos are everywhere and these guys are lethal! Be sure to get some bug spray and lather yourself. Avoid perfumes or scented creams to keep them away! - there's a coral sanctuary nearby which is 3000slr to get to for two people on a speed boat....quite expensive. I asked someone who did it and he said it wasn't anything wow so we opted out and preferred to spend the money on eating.- a few dress shops around and a great buy. The fabric is super cool for the hot weather and its extremely comfortable. We walked into a shop with an older lady and her daughter and grand daughter. We saw two dresses hanging and they offered to make it for us with a fabric of our choice! We spent 1500slr and 2500slr. We didn't bargain on this because we got a deal on a custom made dress!! Highly recommended! The lady didnt even measure us! We explained some adjustments we wanted and when we went back the next day the dresses fit perfectly!

body: The worst of sri lanka : expensive activities, crowded beach during high season, beach boys nice at the beginning, very agressive after. I rent for one hour for my young daughter a small bodyboard (800 Rs), which was already in bad shape. When we finished our hour, the beach lady asked me to pay the board since she said we broke it. As I did not want, she turned very fast very agressive, threated us.It surprised me,since I never saw people so upset in sri lanka ( except maybe on the road!). The show was well prepared and she even called a policeman! We finished by giving 1000 to be able to leave but I guess the board is again at rental and they will ask the same to every tourist. Very bad experience, be careful with these beach people. Check well the stuff you rent, do not let your child taking it without checking. The beach ladies are on the left, just after the entrance to the beach. Very low level people. The local mafia. There are some surf lessons. Same stuff as above, if you want to learn surf, take a real lesson, not what I have seen ( it was so funny to see all these people paying a few thousands to get very bad surf advises).You should better go a bit further, there are many beaches nicer, with almost nobody.

body: Our hotel was a rather small one a bit out of the city centre. Therefore the beach was rather empty. It was lovely and clean. We went up to the snorkling spots to hikkaduwa town, which was nice too. But really busy even though the high season only starts next month. The snorkling around the beach was nice, nothing crazy special but enjoyable. We would not recommend to pay a guide to bring you out to the rocks for a snorkel trip as you don't really see anything. It was 50usd without gear from 9am to 11am. Which meant we met at the office at 9 then walked about 15 min to the catamaran to bring us out, which took another 15min. The guy then called us back in and told us we could stay out but would have to pay extra. Anyway we went back in and by the time we got back to the beach we realised it wasn't even close to 11am. We therefore paid 40usd (as we had our own gear) for maybe 45min of snorkling. Which was a waste of money.
title: Not too crowded but don't pay for snorkling.

body: Sri Lanka was a beautiful country, which gave me amazing experiences I will always cherish. However, Hikkaduwa was not one of them. This is a long review, but worth the read in my opinion. As a fan of marine life, I immediately looked for options for snorkeling and diving in Hikkaduwa beach. We happened upon this snorkeling tour company on the beach and decided to go snorkeling with them. My friend and I are good swimmers but they were quite insistent on sending a professional (independent) lifeguard with each of us. The lifeguards were quite helpful in spotting fish and other sea creatures and in guiding us through the fairly choppy water. At first they would steady us by holding our hand or placing their hands on our shoulders (all well and good). However, my appointed lifeguard started putting his hand on my waist and then lowering it and cupping my bum. The first time this happened I thought maybe it was a mistake and pushed his hand away but he continued to do this. When I stopped him and clearly told him I didn't like it and to stop, he pretended like he couldn't understand what I was saying. When he realised I was clearly quite angry/upset he stopped. But when I was swimming I felt a hand on my stomach creeping lower and lower until he was actually grabbing my crotch. I immediately pushed him away and he immediately did it again-I couldn't physically overpower him and he continued touching me inappropriately until I swam away from him. I tried swimming away from him as fast as I could but he kept pace so I went back to the boat and sat there in complete silence waiting for us to get back to the beach.When we reached the beach I tried explaining what happened to other people on the beach and to the tour operator that we went with and none of them understood. The lifeguard in question even had the cheek to ask me if I was single and wanted to try out a Sri Lankan man. After I firmly declined, he demanded a 1000 rupees tip, for sexually assaulting me, and followed us down the beach until we physically ran away from him. I don't know his name or remember the tour company's name but I wanted to at least warn any female travellers to be very careful of and to try and completely avoid these so-called "lifeguards".Hikkaduwa seemed to be another world of its own. It was filled with lecherous men constantly making advances to us and assuming that as two female travellers we were interested in some sort of sexual awakening that we were sure as hell not interested in.
title: WRITING THIS FOR ALL FEMALE TRAVELLERS

Beautiful but litter strewn
body: Like the towns in Sri Lanka, the lack of waste management extended to the beach which I found quite heartbreaking. I managed to take a few photos editing out the litter and a couple showing the litter.Hikkaduwa Beach could be a beautiful, tropical paradise but the rubbish strewn along big parts of it and what looked like sewage spewing into the ocean at high tide near the Hikka Tranz hotel, was terrible.On a positive note, the ocean was warm and clean and we snorkeled near the Hikkaduwa Beach Hotel first thing in the morning for clearer visibility. There were quite a number of fish swimming around our feet so it was very accessible. There were quite a few beachfront restaurants but we found the Sunset Coffee Bar near the Hikkaduwa Tranz, to be the best, serving delicious Sri Lankan and Western food.Turtles: such beautiful creatures, pity some people don't let them be. One or two come in at low tide near the Hikkaduwa Tranz hotel and when we passed by, a local was selling seaweed to tourists to feed to the turtle. It was pretty shocking to watch people grabbing the turtle and trying to stuff seaweed into its face and holding it to stop it heading out to sea just so they could get the best photos. We also saw someone try to ride a turtle when we were snorkeling but we were too far away to say something. I really felt quite uncomfortable with all this.

title: Fantastic beach with fine golden sand and great snorkelling.
body: Hikkaduwa beach was a great surprise. The sand was fine and golden. We were able to snorkel with ease with the children as there were many areas where the sea was waist deep with plenty of fish to see a few metres out from the shore. At the top end of the beach there was a corner which was visited every day by sea turtles which was an amazing experience for children and adults alike. You do need to be careful walking along the mid beach area with small children as the shore is very narrow and the waves can get quite high. It is easy to arrange diving and snorkelling expeditions via the many companies along the beach but be careful to choose official providers equipped with ladders to get back into the boats as this is where we got caught short and we found it very difficult to get back into our glass bottommed boat without a ladder, resulting in a few scrapes from barnacles attached to the bottom of the boat.

body: I have travelled to this beach three time now, 2002, 2004 and again this past April 2017. In all my travels and the many beaches I have seen Hikkaduwa beach is in my opinion the best. I love to walk on the beach and on this beach you can walk forever. There is also fantastic snorkelling. The restaurants on the beach have amazing food at cheap prices. My favourite part of this beach is the beautiful sunsets. I hope that I will get the chance to visit Hikkaduwa Beach at least one more time in my life.
